title: Answer granularity and date-form alternatives

prompts.J_A: Audit each candidate equally; C0 is not privileged and later candidates are not automatically wrong. Distinguish ANSWER FORM from FACT. Date-order variants with identical day/month/year can describe one fact; they are not contradictions. A calendar label cannot safely be dropped without checking calendar semantics. Year-only and full-date strings can have different granularity but may describe the same event. Positive subject-relation-object assignments are support, not counterevidence. For every date check birth versus death versus award/publication; for every artist check performer versus author/producer/chart. Multiple allowed entities may have separate answers. Use wrong_argument only for an explicit different role/type, not an unfamiliar value or alternate valid referent. Do not treat candidate inventory as an answer key.
prompts.J_B: Conservative audit with a granularity check. Verify each candidate against ALL original segments. A directly stated second artist, second namesake birth date or second sport is direct even if it is not the first candidate. Positive statement goes in support; counter is only actual incompatible evidence for that exact referent, never a support sentence relabeled negative. Equivalent date forms are not competing facts. Do not reject a date merely because wording or calendar notation differs. Likewise do not admit a loose synonym, associated person or more detailed date as a NEW independent answer. Respect the exact requested answer type; cities cannot answer when-born. Keep unresolved factual reliability separate from role errors.
prompts.M07: Return a minimal COMPLETE set: one concise representative per distinct semantic answer, not every string that seems related. Preserve original R5 wording when that answer is valid. Reject equivalent alternative strings rather than outputting both, including year-plus-full-date for the same event or broad-plus-specific sports names. Extra answer text can make a correct set wrong. An actual additional namesake/artist is a distinct answer and must be preserved. Date-order alternatives are available only to clarify representation; never turn one date into another or silently change calendar. Check each candidate against requested role and exact event; a birthplace, creator of a song or chart appearance is not a born-date or performer answer. Add only a distinct missing answer with direct contextual support.
prompts.M08: Selection is a set-completeness task, not a list of all supported strings. Work through each allowed entity/referent, identify its exact requested relation, then choose one short supplied candidate representing that answer. Prefer a valid saved R5 surface form over redundant aliases. Do not add both a year and a full date for the same event, or equivalent alternate date orders. Keep all different valid namesakes and artists. Reject supplementary facts about other roles, population projections, citations, charts and associated cities. Do not assume every proposed candidate is valid. Calendar qualifier stripping is not automatic proof of same meaning; use originals. Do not replace a complete set with only its first or most familiar answer.
prompts.M10: Original documents, candidate inventory and saved R5 answers are supplied; original cards are deliberately omitted in this variant. Revise R5 conservatively and return the complete minimal short-answer set. Choose one representative per semantic answer, preserving valid R5 strings. Do not emit both synonyms or both year and full-date forms for one event. Preserve all separately valid referents, and reject the wrong event, role, author instead of performer, incidental location, or projected population instead of the requested population. A date-order alternative must retain identical components; do not silently remove a calendar distinction. Add only distinct missing directly supported answers, and do not treat candidate generation as evidence.

lesson_response: R3 protected union retained all reference items but lost8 previously strict-correct cases through redundant forms/irrelevant extras (2gains). R4 aliases are same date components/reordered strings plus qualifier stripping proposals only, not certified calendar equivalence. All stages see all originals; M07/M08 omit audit labels; M10 also omits original_cards only (saved R5/candidates still contain upstream card influence, so NOT a pure no-card causal ablation). M09 protects R5 and admits only selector intersection extras; never per-question score selection. Flags/prompts/pool change as an adaptive bundle.
